_comment: WHAT THE GAME TEACHES ABOUT ITSELF, and when.

Kent, playing Level 1: 'its just knowledge dumping at this point, i feel so overwhelmed, why are the instructions popping everywhere ... when there is instructions it is better that the screen goes dim and then that part is highlighted'. And before that: 'not like those just text but add visuals like the button itself ... there are players that will play it without reading it'.

So a lesson is a CARD in one of two places (top or bottom centre, away from what it is about), over a dimmed screen with a hole lit where the lesson is, and the card is first a PICTURE -- `visual` -- of the key or mouse doing the thing, then a short `caption`. TutorialSpotlight draws it; TutorialDirector decides when. One at a time, a breath between them, nothing over anyone talking.

`mode`: `do` lessons keep the world running and go the moment the player presses what they show (the press still does its job); `look` lessons stop the world -- they are about a reading that moves, the clock, the ink -- and any key or click dismisses them. `say` is Lolo remarking rather than the game instructing, and goes to his hint bar over the apo.
`delay` is how long a lesson waits, once its moment has come, before it shows. If the player does the thing in that time it is spent unshown: a player who walks at once is never told how to walk.

`context` is when a lesson may show; `anchor` is what it lights up, resolved by LevelBase._tutorial_target. A lesson whose context or anchor does not hold waits for it, and gives up after `patience` seconds (default 8) to be offered again by its event. A `say` reminder also gives up if it waits too long for the hint bar.

KEYS ARE NOT WRITTEN HERE. `action` (plus `through` for a pair or a numbered run) is read off the live InputMap and drawn as caps, so a rebinding cannot leave a lesson showing a key that no longer does anything. `mouse` lists the mouse inputs a lesson teaches: left, right, wheel, shift_wheel. `text` is the full sentence, still what the hint bar says when there is no spotlight, and what the audits read.

NO LESSON MAY NAME A DRAWABLE CLASS, in its text or its caption. Same rule as the dialogue: `key`, `door`, `wheel` are all classes and all answers somewhere. The pictures follow it too: 'your drawing' is drawn as a scrap of paper with a scribble on it, never a shape.

`at` is the event that offers a lesson; `after` holds it back until another has been spent, so the order survives a player who does things out of sequence. Cut on this pass because they were the dumping: `pause` (Escape is the one key everybody already knows; taught again, at the door, because its list of controls is where a player who forgets a card goes), `sure` (the confidence number is shown on the card; explaining it at the second second of a ten-second life was a third card in a row), `sign` (the E READ prompt already says it), and the canvas briefing, four lines of Lolo inside the panel -- the canvas is now taught by two cards that only appear if the player hesitates.

`lead` is what Lolo says in the story box BEFORE a card shows, so the card answers something he asked: 'Come, apo, walk with me' and then the keys. Said once, through TutorialDirector.bind_lead. Not used on `say` lessons (they are Lolo already) or on the canvas, whose story box is hidden under the drawing panel -- the `draw` lesson leads into it. Cards do not play at all on a return visit.

LEVEL 1 TEACHES THE GAME; A LATER LEVEL ONLY SAYS WHAT IT CHANGES. Kent: 'fix level 1 like tutorial part make sure it covers everything and other levels wont have any tutorials if necessary'. run_tutorial_audit holds both halves: every control that works in Level 1 has a lesson here, and a later level may show a card only for a rule or control Level 1 cannot teach. Everything else a later level says goes to the hint bar (`say`), which dims nothing and stops nothing.

`carries` IS WHAT A ROUTE CAN MISS. Most of Level 1's lessons wait for the player to do the thing, and a run can finish it having never become anything. A `carries` lesson still unspent when the level ends is owed (PlayerProfile.lessons_owed) and is shown once, the first time its moment comes in a later level, without its `lead`: Lolo is not in every level, and nobody there was building up to it. A press on SKIP TUTORIAL owes nothing. A lesson that is not true everywhere (`undo`, `ink`: the ink rules change) does not carry.

WHAT CAN BE TAUGHT AT THE START IS, AT THE DOOR; THE REST IN ITS MOMENT. Kent: 'the tutorial should pop up for when the moment happens but there should be tutorial that is appropriate at the start like the movement, inventory, jump, etc'. Once level_1's opening has been said, its `door` lessons -- about what is already there: walking, jumping, the bag and its face-down cards, the quest card, the arrow, the map, Escape -- play back to back, in the order they are listed here, with no `lead` and no `delay`, lighting their `entry_anchor` (TutorialDirector.teach_the_door, LevelBase._teaches_at_the_door). `entry_live` ones are done for real: walking and jumping with the world running, and the click on a face-down card in the bag; the rest hold the world. A card with `entry_opens` opens it for real when done: Tab on the bag's card opens the bag, and the next card is shown over it (`context: bag`), lighting a face-down card to click (`click_on_it`). Every other lesson waits for its moment, as before. (For a day all of them played at the door, and taught a canvas, a placed drawing and a creature that were not there.) A block with `strict` (level_1's) has every card WAIT FOR THE PLAYER TO DO IT -- Kent: 'when the tutorial says press R, when i press another key, it just proceeds to the next one, it does not let me experience the tutorial'. A strict card goes only on its own key or click (a `look` card with nothing to press, on a click or Enter), with a tick, or when what it lights goes: no timeout, no other key.

lessons.caption: Walk
lessons.text: Walk with me, apo. {keys}.
lessons.lead: Come, apo. Walk with me — the terraces will not wait for us.

lessons.caption: Jump
lessons.text: {keys} to jump.
lessons.lead: Can you still jump, apo? Show me — the way up is never flat for long.

lessons.caption: Hold to climb
lessons.text: Stand at it and hold {keys}, apo. That is how you go up.
lessons.lead: There — something to go up. Hold on tight and climb.

lessons.caption: Draw something
lessons.text: Her brush is in here. {keys} opens it.
lead: That wall is too tall to walk up.
Her brush is in your hand. Open her canvas, draw what you need, then Paint it — whatever you paint, this place believes.

lessons.caption: Draw with the mouse
lessons.text: Draw with the mouse, apo.

lessons.caption: Done? Press Paint
lessons.text: Then Paint it, apo.

lessons.caption: Move to aim. Click to set it down
lessons.text: Mouse aims. Left click sets it down.
lessons.lead: Now set it where you need it. Aim it, and put it down gently.

lessons.caption: Make it bigger or smaller
lessons.text: {keys} make it smaller and bigger. So does scrolling with Shift held.
lessons.lead: Too big? Too small? You can change its size before you let go.

lessons.caption: Turn it
lessons.text: {keys} turns it. So does scrolling.
lessons.lead: And you can turn it, too — tilt it until it sits right.

lessons.caption: Right-click takes it back, ink and all
lessons.text: Right click takes it back, and the ink with it.
lessons.lead: Changed your mind? You can always take a drawing back.

lessons.caption: Every drawing costs ink
lessons.text: That cost ink, apo. There is not much of it.
lessons.lead: Her brush runs on ink, apo, and we do not have much. Spend it wisely.

lessons.caption: Draw something alive and you become it
lessons.text: Draw something alive, apo, and you become it.
lessons.lead: One more thing, apo. Paint something alive and you do not carry it. You become it.

lessons.caption: It runs out
lessons.text: That bar is the drawing's life, apo. It runs out.
lessons.lead: Watch that bar, apo. Something you become does not last forever.

lessons.caption: Change back to yourself
lessons.text: {keys} puts you back as yourself.
lessons.lead: You can always come back to yourself, apo. Remember how.

lessons.caption: Tap it again and again to rise
lessons.text: {keys}, again and again, keeps you in the air.
lessons.lead: You have to work for the sky, apo. Keep beating, or down you come.

lessons.caption: Swim up and down
lessons.text: {keys} take you up and down in the water.
lessons.lead: The water will have you now, apo. Go as deep as you like.

lessons.caption: Pick up or use what is near
lessons.text: {keys} picks up or uses whatever is near you, apo.
lessons.lead: See that key over your head? It works on whatever you are standing near.

lessons.caption: Use what you hold
lessons.text: {keys} uses it.
lessons.lead: You are holding it now. Go on, apo, use it.

lessons.caption: Take it out of your bag
lessons.text: In your bag. {keys} brings it out.
lessons.lead: You kept it. Good — whatever goes in your bag, you can bring out again.

lessons.caption: Drag a drawing out of your bag
lessons.text: Pull a drawing off its slot, apo, and let go where you want it.

lessons.caption: Open your bag
lessons.text: {keys} opens your bag, apo. It remembers everything you draw.
lessons.lead: Your bag remembers everything you have ever drawn. Have a look inside sometime.

lessons.caption: Click a face-down card for a hint
lessons.text: A card you have not drawn yet hints at what to draw. Click one, apo.

lessons.caption: Fall, and you start again here
lessons.text: That lantern is a checkpoint, apo. If you fall or get stuck, you start again from here, with the ink you had.
lessons.lead: A lantern! She lit these so nobody would lose their way.

lessons.caption: Your next task is always here
lessons.text: The card at the top says what comes next, apo.
lessons.lead: If you ever lose your way, apo, look up. That card says what comes next.

lessons.caption: What it needs DONE, not drawn
lessons.text: That word is what it needs DONE, not what to draw.
lessons.lead: See that word? It tells you what must be DONE here — not what to draw.

lessons.caption: The arrow points the way
lessons.text: That arrow points to what comes next, apo.

lessons.caption: The map shows where you went
lessons.text: The map in the corner shows where you have been, apo.

lessons.caption: Pause, and see all the controls
lessons.text: {keys} stops everything, and lists all the controls.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: It is going, apo. A drawing does not last.

$comment: DAGAT TEACHES ONE THING, AND IT REPLACES SOMETHING THE PLAYER ALREADY LEARNED.
Level 1 taught 'that bar is the drawing's life, apo -- it runs out'. Dagat takes the
clock away and charges ink instead, and a player who has been told the first thing and
not the second will read a draining bar as the same ten seconds and plan against a
rule that no longer exists.
⚠ NONE OF THESE FIRE FROM MorphLife. level_1's 'clock' and 'life' lessons hang on
morph_running and morph_low, which LevelBase notes from _on_life_changed -- and Dagat
answers _morph_has_a_life() with false, so that signal never comes. level_3.gd emits
its own events off InkDrain instead. An event nothing notes is a lesson nobody gets.
The shore is where all of this lands, before the fork. The design is firm about why:
once the player is underwater, learning the ink rule by running out of it is a
punishment rather than a lesson.
TWO CARDS, AND ONLY TWO. `new_brush` carries the whole rule and `jars` the one way to
refill, because neither can be taught anywhere else. The drain, the free change back
and running low are reminders of what the card already said, so they are lines on the
bar. ⚠ A line on the bar waits for the bar, and Lolo is on it for most of the dive, so
nothing the player cannot do without may live only there: that is why `jars` stays a card.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.caption: Holding a shape spends ink, not time
lessons.text: Hers counted you down. This one spends ink the whole time you hold a shape.
lessons.lead: A new brush! Hers counted the time down... this one is different.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: That bar is your ink now, apo. It goes down the whole time you are holding the shape.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: {keys} puts you back, and stops it going down. Changing back never costs.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: You are nearly out. It does not come back on its own out here — you have to find more of it.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: Up you come. You lost the crossing, not anything else. Go again.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.text: Only what belongs down here will hold, apo. Anything else will start drowning on you.

lessons.speaker: Lolo
lessons.caption: Swim through a jar to fill up
lessons.text: Those jars on the bottom are ink. Swim through one and this fills back up.
lessons.lead: Look down there, apo! Those jars on the seabed — they are full of ink.

$comment: DILIM TEACHES WHAT IS NEW ABOUT A FIGHT, AND NOTHING ELSE.
Lolo is not here, so every lesson is hers (`speaker` Apo) and none has a `lead`: there is
nobody to ask the question a card answers. Two cards with pictures, for what Level 1 cannot
teach because it does nothing there -- the lamp that is her life and the click that swings
-- and lines on the hint bar, which never stops play, for the rest: the ink every drawing
costs, the first hit to the lantern, and a weapon nearly worn through.
Every event is level_4.gd's or LevelBase's: weapon_in_hand and weapon_wearing are polled
off the weapon in her hand, lantern_hit is the lantern's own signal, ink_spent is the
base's; santelmo_near is a burning santelmo within sight of her, which is where walking
with Shift is taught -- where it matters. ON THE HINT BAR, NOT A CARD: a card dims all but
her, and the flame it is about would vanish under its own warning.
THE LAMP IS TAUGHT BEFORE THE FIRST FIGHT. Kent found the fights and the lamp confusing: its
only lesson came at the first hit, on the bar, mid-fight. So at the first clearing -- where the
lamp is filled, past the santelmo and before the sigbin -- a card lights the lantern on the ink
plate and shows it: the HUD's own lamp, dimming a stage a hit, then her back at the last lit
lantern. NOT AT HER FIRST STEPS: there it held the queue, and the santelmo's walk lesson came
too late, under the card's dim. The first hit still says it, on the bar.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.text: Never run from a santelmo. Hold {keys} and walk, and it loses interest.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.caption: Every hit dims the lamp
lessons.text: This lamp is my life out here. Every hit dims it, and if it goes out I go back to where it was last lit.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.caption: Click where you want to swing
lessons.text: A click, and I swing at whatever is there.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.text: Out here every drawing costs ink, even one I have drawn before. The clearings fill it back up.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.text: Every hit dims the lamp. If it goes out, I go back to where it was last lit.

lessons.speaker: Apo
lessons.text: This one is nearly worn through. When it goes, I draw another.
